{{nihongo|'''Kuga Shrine'''|久我神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following deity is enshrined: {{Sfn|Kamigamo Shrine (Student Shrine)|2003|pp=51-52}}.
* '''{{ill|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|it|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|ja|賀茂建角身命|zh|賀茂建角身命|qid=Q11634939}}''' (Kamotake Tsunumi Mikoto)
*: Ancestor god of {{ill|Kamo clan|Q2975287|qid=Q2975287|lt=Kamo Prefectural Lord}} (Kamo clan). He was the grandfather of Kamigamo Shrine's enshrined deity, {{ill|Kamo-wake-ikazuchi-no-Kami|Q11634943|qid=Q11634943}} (Kamowakeikazuchi no Mikoto), {{jalink|Emperor Jimmu|Q2001 It is identified with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ar|ياتاغاراسو|bcl|Yatagarasu|br|Yatagarasu|cs|Jatagarasu|de|Yatagarasu|es|Yatagarasu|fa|یاتاگاراسو|fr|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏|ko|야타가라스|la|Yatagarasu|no|Yatagarasu|pl|Yatagarasu|ru|Ятагарасу|simple|Yatagarasu|uk|Ятаґарасу|zh|八咫烏|qid=Q745463}} (Yatagarasu) who led the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Q11590444|qid=Q11590444|lt=Tosei}} in 88}}.

Since ancient times the company name has been called ``Uji Shrine'', the enshrined deity is said to be Kamo Takekaku no Mikoto, the ancestral deity of the Kamo clan, but according to Kamigamo Shrine documents, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Early modern}} also had different theories such as {{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Q478504|qid=Q478504|lt=Kuni no Tokodateson}} {{Sfn|Kuga Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.

Founding date is unknown. Our company is believed to be one of the shrines {{Sfn|Kuga Shrine (Gods)|1985}} that was enshrined by {{ill|Kamo clan|Q2975287|qid=Q2975287}} when he moved from {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato}} to {{ill|Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276|lt=Yamashiro}}. "{{ill|Fudoki|Q1194534|qid=Q1194534|lt=Yamashiro no Kuni Fudoki}}" Isshu <ref group="original">Isshu of "Yamashiro no Kuni Fudoki" quoted in volume 9 of "Shaku Nihongi". According to </ref>, after Kamo Kenkakumi no Mikoto achieved great success in Emperor Jimmu's eastern expedition, he moved from Yamato to ``Kamo in Okada, Yamashiro Province'', ``Kazuno River ({{ill|Katsura River|Q2909307|qid=Q2909307|lt=Katsura River}}) and Kamo River ({{jalink|Kamogawa River}). (Kyoto Prefecture) | Q27218 | Kamogawa}})" and "Yamamoto in the north of Kuga no Kuni", and the guardian deities of the Kamo clan are still enshrined at each location {{Sfn|Kuga Shrine (Gods) | 1985}}. The specific locations for each location are as follows.# Kamo, Okada, Yamashiro no Kuni - present-day Kamo Town, Kyoto Prefecture {{ill|Kizugawa, Kyoto|Q990352|qid=Q990352}}. The {{ill|Okada Kamo Shrine|Q11473738|qid=Q11473738}} ({{Coord|34|45|41.55|N|135|52|34.92|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|name=1. Okada Kamo Shrine}}) of {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} is enshrined here.

The Shikinai shrine, Kuga Shrine (currently {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kuga Shrine}}, {{Coord|34|56|26.37|N|135|43|48.94|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|name=2. Kuga Shrine (currently Kuga Shrine)}}) is located there.
# Yamamoto in the north of Kuga no Kuni - near our company.
Regarding the place name "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kuga (country)}}", there is a theory that it is an old name for the entire area, but it declined as the Kamo clan's influence spread, but it was originally the name of {{ill|Otokuni District, Kyoto|Q376858|qid=Q376858}}, where Kuga Shrine (Kuga Shrine) is located. There is a theory that the name was followed in this area, and another theory that the original name is {{ill|Kii district|Q11604966|qid=Q11604966}} of Minamiyama Castle, not Otokuni-gun.

There is a tradition that our company was enshrined at its current location because there was a tomb of Kenkaku Kamo no Mikoto nearby, but this is not clear {{Sfn|Kamigamo Shrine (Student Shrine)|2003|pp=51-52}}

=== God level ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} January 27, 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from upper 6th rank to lower rank of 5th rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Kugagami.''

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Kuga-jinja2.JPG|thumb|200px|A zelkova stump<br />{{Smaller|The tree is said to be 600 years old.{{Sfn|Kamigamo Shrine (Student Shrine)|2003|pp=51-52}}. }}]]
In the ``{{ill|Yongshu Fushi|ja|雍州府志|qid=Q18460389}}'' written in 1686|Q7664}}, the precincts are commonly referred to as the ``Omiya Forest,'' and there are still giant {{ill|Zelkova serrata|Q920344|qid=Q920344}} trees on the premises that still bear traces of that past.<ref name="Explanation board"/>. The temple grounds have been designated as a Kyoto City designated historic site, as the tradition of the migration of the Kamo clan has been passed down to the present day, and the environment that reveals the history of Kyoto has been preserved in good condition.

The current main shrine and worship hall were built in {{ill|Kan'ei|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}}5 ({{ill|1628|Q6840|qid=Q6840}}){{Sfn|Kamigamo Shrine (Student Shrine)|2003|pp=51-52}}. The main shrine is in the style of Ikken-sha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}, with a {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|zh|檜皮葺|qid=Q90373477}} roof, and is the same structure as other shrines of Kamigamo Shrine<ref name="Explanation board"/>. The worship hall has a {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} gable with one beam and two beams, and the roof is also thatched with cypress bark.Furthermore, there is a legend that Kuga Shrine was called ``Omiya'' from the time of its establishment, and that the name of the area was ``Omiya'' (Omiya-go) and the street name in front of the gate was ``Omiya-dori.'' That street is {{ill|Daitokuji Street|Q11435442|qid=Q11435442}}, which locals still refer to as ``Old Omiya-dori'' today.

* Shinko Festival ({{ill|November 3|Q2995|qid=Q2995}}) - {{ill|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi}} parades through the shrine parishioners of the four former Omiya-go school districts (Omiya, Taiho, Shichiku, and Motomachi).

During the spring and autumn festivals, a ritual called ``Hikiuma-nogi'' is held in which Kamigamo Shrine's sacred horse circles the main shrine three times.
